articles.headline: El 'triángulo sísmico' de Lugo: Sarria, Triacastela y Becerreá concentran los mayores terremotos de la provincia
articles.subtitle: Sarria, Triacastela y Becerreá concentran más de la mitad de los seísmos que se registran cada año en Galicia. El Progreso repasa la historia sísmica de la montaña lucense, desde el terremoto de Guilfrei de 1997 hasta el derrumbe de la catedral de Lugo en 1755.
articles.body:
Sarria, Triacastela y Becerreá forman lo que los sismólogos llaman el 'triángulo sísmico' de Lugo: la zona de la provincia donde se concentran más de la mitad de los terremotos que se registran cada año en Galicia. El Progreso repasa esta semana la historia sísmica de la montaña lucense, en plena semana de réplicas en Granada.

El episodio más reciente de importancia fue el terremoto de Guilfrei, en Triacastela, del 22 de mayo de 1997: con magnitud 5,1, se sintió en toda Galicia y en el oeste de Castilla y León y provocó un fallecimiento por infarto en Becerreá.

Antes, en 1995, la zona ya había registrado seísmos de 4,7 en Baralla y Triacastela, y en 1979 uno de 4,6 en Sarria causó daños y pánico, con vecinos que salieron despavoridos incluso de la catedral de Lugo.

La falla de Becerreá, de unos 40 kilómetros de longitud y hasta 9.000 metros de profundidad, es la gran responsable. El Instituto Geográfico Nacional recoge estos episodios en su catálogo de terremotos importantes, y el riesgo actual se considera mínimo: Galicia es zona de riesgo sísmico desde 2002 y cuenta con el plan Sismigal y una red de sismógrafos portátiles.

La memoria histórica va más lejos: el terremoto de Lisboa de 1755, de magnitud 8,5, derribó la bóveda central y la fachada oeste de la catedral de Lugo. Mientras tanto, la actividad sísmica de Granada sigue copando titulares, lo que reaviva la curiosidad por el subsuelo de la provincia.

articles.headline: La sequía aprieta a la ganadería de Lugo: cisternas para las lácteas y 52,5 millones en pérdidas de forrajes
articles.subtitle: Lactalis traslada agua a su planta de Vilalba y Larsa empezará a tomar suministro en Outeiro de Rei. UU.AA. cifra en 52,5 millones las pérdidas en forrajes y pastos de la provincia, y el Miño baja con seis grados más de temperatura que hace veinte años.
articles.body:
La sequía empieza a notarse en la industria láctea de Lugo. Lactalis, que tiene planta en Vilalba, ha comenzado a completar sus necesidades de agua con traslados en cisterna a la fábrica, mientras que Larsa empezará a tomar suministro en la captación de Outeiro de Rei, según informa La Voz de Galicia.

En el campo, las pérdidas se acumulan: la organización agraria UU.AA. cifra en 52,5 millones de euros las pérdidas en forrajes y pastos en la provincia de Lugo a causa de la falta de lluvias, una factura que condicionará la alimentación del ganado este invierno.

El río Azúmara, a su paso por Castro de Rei, muestra un caudal muy bajo, y el Miño a su paso por Lugo refleja también el estiaje: la temperatura del agua ha subido seis grados en veinte años, en contraste con el alto nivel de los ríos de otras zonas como Cataluña.

Las industrias aseguran que, por ahora, el abastecimiento está garantizado y que las cisternas son una medida preventiva, pero admiten que la situación exige vigilancia si el otoño no trae lluvias.

articles.headline: Alarma en la calzada romana de Lugo por un fuego en una finca abandonada llena de maleza
articles.subtitle: Un incendio en una finca abandonada junto a la calzada romana de Lugo puso en alerta a los vecinos, que denuncian solares llenos de maleza. Horas antes, un fuego en O Carqueixo quemó chatarra y electrodomésticos con una gran humareda.
articles.body:
Los vecinos de la zona de la calzada romana de Lugo viven con preocupación cada verano: este miércoles, un fuego declarado en una finca abandonada llena de maleza junto a la vía romana obligó a movilizar a los bomberos, que lograron sofocarlo antes de que se propagara.

Los residentes llevan tiempo denunciando la acumulación de maleza y basura en solares abandonados del entorno, que consideran un riesgo evidente de incendio en plena ola de calor. El Concello recuerda que los propietarios están obligados a mantener limpios sus terrenos.

El aviso llegó el mismo día en que un incendio en O Carqueixo, en las afueras de la ciudad, quemó chatarra, electrodomésticos inservibles y botes de pintura, con varios focos y una gran columna de humo visible desde distintos puntos de Lugo. El fuego se extendió durante horas y no se dio por extinguido hasta las 00.38 de la madrugada.

Las llamas, alimentadas por material inflamable abandonado, requirieron un amplio despliegue de bomberos y de la Consellería do Medio Rural. Ninguno de los dos incendios causó heridos.

articles.headline: Galicia pasa del verano al otoño en un día: caída de diez grados y lluvias débiles
articles.subtitle: Galicia pasa del verano al otoño en un día: la caída de temperaturas alcanza los diez grados y Lugo bajará de los 32 a los 22 grados, con lluvias débiles y ambiente otoñal hasta el fin de semana.
articles.body:
El verano ha hecho un paréntesis en Galicia. La comunidad pasó en apenas 24 horas de los 32,5 grados de Lugo a máximas de 22, una caída de diez grados que la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) atribuye a la entrada de aire fresco del Atlántico.

El cambio, adelantado por Meteogalicia con avisos en el litoral, trae además lluvias débiles y persistentes, sobre todo en la mitad norte, y un ambiente otoñal que se mantendrá al menos hasta el fin de semana.

La tregua térmica da un respiro tras una semana de calor intenso y agrava el contraste con la sequía: los embalses y los ríos de la comunidad siguen en niveles bajos y las lluvias previstas serán insuficientes para revertir el déficit hídrico.

Para los próximos días, AEMET prevé temperaturas suaves, con máximas que no superarán los 25 grados en la provincia de Lugo y noches frescas, antes de un posible repunte del calor a principios de la próxima semana.

articles.headline: La Policía desaloja la playa del Trampolín en Ceuta y los migrantes vuelven a instalarse horas después
articles.subtitle: La Policía Nacional desalojó la playa del Trampolín, donde se concentraban entre 3.500 y 5.000 migrantes, y los trasladó a espacios con capacidad para 1.800 personas. Horas después, cientos volvían a instalarse en el arenal.
articles.body:
La crisis migratoria de Ceuta encadena su tercera semana con un nuevo episodio: la Policía Nacional desalojó este jueves la playa del Trampolín, donde se concentraban entre 3.500 y 5.000 migrantes, según la estimación policial, y los derivó a espacios temporales como Loma Margarita y El Embolsamiento.

La ministra de Inclusión, Elma Saiz, confirmó que el dispositivo tiene capacidad para unas 1.800 personas, ampliable con otras instalaciones como la Hípica, el campo de fútbol del antiguo cuartel de caballería o El Guano. El desalojo transcurrió sin incidentes y a media mañana la zona estaba en calma.

Horas después, cientos de migrantes volvían a instalarse en el arenal, evidenciando la dificultad de dar una solución de fondo. El Gobierno trabaja en el traslado de unos 500 menores a la península, mientras el PP reclama que también sean expulsados, algo que el Ejecutivo considera ilegal al tratarse de menores.

La situación se enquista mientras la oposición pide la reprobación de cinco ministros por la gestión de la crisis, y las organizaciones humanitarias advierten de las condiciones de hacinamiento en los nuevos espacios.

articles.headline: El incendio de Las Hurdes arrasa ya 4.800 hectáreas y el tiempo da una tregua para atacarlo por aire
articles.subtitle: El incendio de Las Hurdes ha arrasado ya 4.800 hectáreas y mantiene un perímetro de 48 kilómetros, con unas 850 personas desalojadas. La mejora del tiempo de este jueves permite reanudar el ataque aéreo contra las llamas.
articles.body:
El incendio forestal de Las Hurdes, en el norte de Cáceres, cumple su tercer día sin control: el fuego ha arrasado ya 4.800 hectáreas y mantiene un perímetro de 48 kilómetros, con cerca de 850 personas desalojadas de sus viviendas en varios municipios.

La tregua meteorológica de este jueves, con menos viento y más humedad, permitió a los medios aéreos reanudar los lanzamientos de agua sobre las llamas, concentradas en el frente de Aldea del Fresno, el más activo desde el inicio del siniestro.

El Centro de Coordinación Operativa (Cecopi) mantiene activado el nivel 2 de peligrosidad y no descarta nuevas evacuaciones si el fuego avanza hacia zonas habitadas. Más de 500 efectivos trabajan en la extinción, apoyados por la Unidad Militar de Emergencias.

El origen del incendio sigue bajo investigación. Los vecinos reclaman más medios de prevención para una comarca muy castigada por los grandes fuegos de los últimos veranos.

articles.headline: La espiral de odio entre los clanes Moriña y Salazar en Isla Cristina deja tres muertos y un bebé nonato
articles.subtitle: La guerra entre los clanes Moriña y Salazar en Isla Cristina se ha cobrado ya la vida de cinco personas: el tiroteo del domingo dejó tres muertos, incluidos un menor y un bebé nonato, y dos heridos, uno grave. La Guardia Civil ha encontrado las armas.
articles.body:
La espiral de violencia entre dos clanes de Isla Cristina, en Huelva, no tiene freno. El tiroteo del pasado domingo en la barriada de El Rocío se saldó con tres muertos: dos mujeres, una de ellas embarazada de ocho meses cuyo bebé nonato también falleció, y un menor de 16 años ajeno al conflicto. Dos personas más resultaron heridas, una de gravedad.

Dos encapuchados llegaron en moto y dispararon con un arma larga antes de huir; la moto y el arma aparecieron quemadas en un pinar cercano. La Guardia Civil ha localizado ahora las armas utilizadas, que serán remitidas al Servicio de Balística, según El Correo Gallego.

El origen está en septiembre de 2024, cuando Manuel Salazar, 'El Baba', mató a su cuñado Ramón Moriña e hirió a otro hombre. En junio de 2025 llegó la primera venganza, con el asesinato del padrastro de Salazar; el domingo se produjo la segunda y más sangrienta.

La investigación, bajo secreto de sumario, intenta determinar quién ordenó el ataque. La familia del menor pide ayuda para esclarecer el crimen y el presidente andaluz, Juanma Moreno, reclama al Gobierno más herramientas contra el narcotráfico en la zona.

articles.headline: La fiebre del Nilo llega a Canarias: tres caballos infectados en Gran Canaria
articles.subtitle: La fiebre del Nilo Occidental llega a Canarias: tres caballos han dado positivo en Gran Canaria tras detectarse el primer foco en San Bartolomé de Tirajana. La expansión del virus, que ya circula en Andalucía, mantiene en alerta a las autoridades sanitarias.
articles.body:
La fiebre del Nilo Occidental ha llegado a Canarias. La Consejería de Sanidad confirmó este jueves que tres caballos han dado positivo en Gran Canaria, después de que el martes se detectara el primer foco de la enfermedad en un équido de San Bartolomé de Tirajana, en el sur de la isla.

Los análisis se activaron tras la aparición de casos en équidos y aves, y los técnicos de Salud Pública han establecido un perímetro de vigilancia alrededor del foco, con 38 animales sensibles bajo control.

El virus, transmitido por mosquitos, preocupa cada vez más en España: este verano ha circulado con fuerza en Andalucía, donde se han registrado casos humanos, y la llegada a Canarias amplía el mapa de la enfermedad, que en los últimos años se ha expandido por el sur de Europa.

En humanos, la mayoría de las infecciones son asintomáticas, pero puede causar encefalitis en personas mayores o con patologías previas. Las autoridades recomiendan eliminar aguas estancadas y protegerse de las picaduras al amanecer y al atardecer.

articles.headline: Seis terremotos marcan la noche en Granada y los vecinos pasan la noche en la calle
articles.subtitle: Seis terremotos marcaron la noche en Granada tras el seísmo de magnitud 4,8 del martes: cinco fueron sentidos por los vecinos, que durmieron en parques y coches por miedo a las réplicas. Los centros de salud recuperan la normalidad.
articles.body:
La tierra no dio tregua en Granada: seis terremotos marcaron la madrugada del miércoles, cinco de ellos sentidos por la población, horas después del seísmo de magnitud 4,8 del martes, el más fuerte registrado en la ciudad en años.

El miedo a las réplicas llevó a muchos vecinos a echarse a la calle y pasar la noche en parques, coches y zonas abiertas del área metropolitana. "Esto acojona mucho, no he dormido nada", contaba un vecino a El País.

La serie sísmica, localizada en el cinturón de fallas del entorno de Granada, mantuvo en alerta a los servicios de emergencia, aunque no se registraron daños personales y solo daños menores en viviendas y mobiliario urbano.

Los centros de salud y hospitales recuperaron este jueves su funcionamiento habitual, y los colegios reanudaron las clases con normalidad. Los expertos del Instituto Geográfico Nacional insisten en que los enjambres sísmicos son habituales en la zona y que no se puede predecir su evolución.

articles.headline: New health minister 'not yet' as Burrows pledges replacement and Robbie Butler emerges as frontrunner
articles.subtitle: First Minister Jon Burrows pledges to name a new Stormont health minister 'but not yet', as Robbie Butler emerges as the frontrunner to replace Mike Nesbitt and Causeway campaigners demand the next minister commit to saving services.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland will get a new health minister, but not immediately. First Minister Jon Burrows has pledged to name a successor to Mike Nesbitt, who resigned on Monday over the handling of the Causeway Hospital row, while insisting the appointment will be made in due course.

Robbie Butler is emerging as the frontrunner, with SDLP MLA Dr Tom Black paying tribute to Nesbitt's difficult job in a divided Executive. Butler, a former firefighter and the DUP's health spokesperson, would inherit a department facing crisis-level pressures.

Causeway Hospital campaigners are pressing the incoming minister to commit to saving services in line with Burrows' own declaration, and argue the row has forced a tipping point in how crucial reform of the health service will be handled.

The appointment is being watched closely across the north-west, where the future of emergency services at Causeway remains the defining political issue of the summer.

articles.headline: Cliftonville members vote 81% in favour of Toronto Investment Group takeover
articles.subtitle: Cliftonville members have voted 81% in favour of a £3 million takeover by the Toronto Investment Group at a special general meeting, clearing the way for the Canadian investors to take control of Ireland's oldest football club.
articles.body:
Cliftonville's future appears settled: members voted in favour of the £3 million takeover by the Toronto Investment Group (TIG) at Monday's extraordinary general meeting, with 81% backing the resolution tabled by chairman Kevin Crossan. A 75% majority was required.

The result ends a long-running saga. Talks were paused last year when former chairman Kieran Harding stepped back, TIG pulled its offer in January, and the issue only resurfaced after a June EGM authorised the management committee to enter formal negotiations.

In a statement, the club said members had attended "the historic poll that has shaped the future of Ireland's oldest football club", and thanked them for their attentive examination of the transaction structure.

The takeover moves ownership of the north Belfast club to the Canadian group, which has pledged investment in the playing squad and facilities.

articles.headline: UFU says resignation demand over Fivemiletown cattle cull is 'not personal' as Muir hits back
articles.subtitle: The Ulster Farmers' Union insists its call for Agriculture Minister Andrew Muir's resignation over the Fivemiletown cattle cull is 'not personal', as the minister accuses the union of trying to dictate government policy.
articles.body:
The Ulster Farmers' Union has insisted its demand for Andrew Muir's resignation is not personal, as the row over the cull of 51 cattle in Fivemiletown, County Tyrone, intensifies. UFU president John McLenaghan said the move was not taken lightly and reflected severely damaged confidence in the department.

The union has also called for the resignation of DAERA Permanent Secretary Katrina Godfrey and Chief Veterinary Officer Brian Dooher over the handling of the June cull, which it says was disproportionate and damaged farmer trust.

Muir hit back, saying "the days of the UFU dictating government policy are over" and arguing the union was opposed to him personally rather than to policy. The FDA union, which represents DAERA vets, said the cull decision was taken by ministers, not officials.

The controversy has exposed deep tensions between the farming community and the Alliance minister, and is unlikely to be resolved before the autumn.

articles.headline: Castlederg's Billy Caldwell, who changed the law on medicinal cannabis, celebrates his 21st birthday
articles.subtitle: Billy Caldwell, the Castlederg teenager whose fight for medicinal cannabis changed UK law in 2018, is celebrating his 21st birthday — three years seizure-free, on an NHS prescription, and thriving.
articles.body:
Billy Caldwell, from Castlederg, County Tyrone, is celebrating his 21st birthday. Born with a severe form of epilepsy that left him with hundreds of seizures a day, Billy's case became a national cause when his cannabis oil was seized at Heathrow in 2018.

The outcry over the seizure of the oil, supplied by his mother Charlotte, prompted a rapid change in the law and a special licence, and Billy became one of the first children in the UK to receive an NHS prescription for cannabis-based medicine.

Now 21, Billy is three years seizure-free, attends college and, according to those close to the family, is thriving. A Harry Potter-themed cake marked the milestone at a celebration attended by family and supporters in the Tyrone town.

The family continues to campaign for wider access to medicinal cannabis for the thousands of other families still fighting for prescriptions.

articles.headline: North Korea fires missile barrage toward the sea after shrugging off Trump's scaled-back drills
articles.subtitle: North Korea fired around ten short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea on Thursday, a day after Pyongyang shrugged off Washington's decision to scale back joint drills with South Korea as an overture 'not even worthy of comment'.
articles.body:
North Korea launched a barrage of missiles toward the sea on Thursday, South Korea's military said, with about ten short-range ballistic missiles fired from the capital region toward eastern waters. Japan said it detected a suspected launch.

The test came a day after the US and South Korea confirmed they were scaling back the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, following Donald Trump's order to substantially reduce them. Trump cited his good relationship with Kim Jong Un and Seoul's refusal to back Washington over the war in Iran.

Kim Yo Jong, the North Korean leader's influential sister, dismissed the overture, saying it was "not even worthy of comment" and that the provocative, aggressive nature of the drills would not change even though their duration and size were reduced.

She denied Trump's claim that Kim had responded to his request for a conversation, while insisting personal relations remain excellent. Trump told reporters he would be meeting Kim this year.

articles.headline: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for wartime presidential election
articles.subtitle: Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's sacked defence minister, has called for wartime presidential elections, saying 'democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia' — the biggest challenge yet to Volodymyr Zelensky's presidency under martial law.
articles.body:
Ukraine's popular former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for wartime presidential elections, in what is widely seen as the biggest challenge to Volodymyr Zelensky's presidency since Russia's full-scale invasion. "Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," Fedorov, 35, said in a video posted on Tuesday.

Ukraine has been under martial law since 2022, which suspends elections. Fedorov, who was unexpectedly dismissed last month just six months after his appointment, did not mention Zelensky by name, but his dismissal sparked protests across the country.

Zelensky has not directly responded, though a source in the presidential office called the election push "highly bizarre" and said it demonstrated a complete lack of realism. Analysts question how voting could be organised for millions of refugees abroad and soldiers on the front line.

Meanwhile, Russia said at least seven people were killed in the largest Ukrainian attack of 2026, and Moscow launched deadly strikes overnight that sparked fires across Kyiv.

articles.headline: Magnitude 7.2 earthquake shakes southern Peru, felt as far as Lima
articles.subtitle: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck southern Peru on Thursday, centred near Coracora in Ayacucho with a depth of 108 kilometres, injuring three people, damaging schools and health centres and cutting power across several districts.
articles.body:
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake shook southern Peru on Thursday afternoon, according to the country's geophysical institute (IGP), with the epicentre 35 kilometres north of Coracora, in the Parinacochas province of Ayacucho, at a depth of 108 kilometres. The US Geological Survey preliminarily estimated the magnitude at 6.7.

The quake was felt with intensity III-IV in at least eight districts and lightly in Lima, more than 600 kilometres away. Authorities reported three injured and damage to 11 schools and 12 health centres, with rockfalls on some mountain roads.

Power outages affected 6,023 users in Nazca and 2,990 in Puquio, while the navy ruled out a tsunami warning. The housing minister travelled to the affected area to coordinate the response.

Peru sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and regularly experiences strong earthquakes; no deaths have been reported so far.

articles.headline: US condemns Israeli airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase as 'unnecessary escalation'
articles.subtitle: The US has condemned Israeli airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase as an 'unnecessary escalation', after eight strikes hit the runway and storage facilities in Idlib province on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The United States has condemned Israeli airstrikes on a Syrian airbase as an unnecessary escalation. Eight strikes hit the runway and storage facilities at Abu al-Duhur, in Syria's Idlib province, on Tuesday; there were no reports of injuries.

Israel justified the strikes by saying Syria was on the verge of breaching the security status quo, citing the presence of Turkish troops near the base. Turkey rejected the allegations, and Syria's foreign ministry called the attack an unjustified act of aggression.

Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and special envoy, said the escalation was unnecessary, though Washington stopped short of sanctions or further action.

The base has been out of service since 2013 and was seized by rebels during their December 2024 offensive. The strikes are among the most significant Israeli operations in Syria since March.

articles.headline: Tesla, Uber and Waymo get the OK to run thousands of robotaxis in Nevada
articles.subtitle: Nevada regulators have unanimously approved permits allowing Tesla, Uber and Waymo to operate up to 8,000 robotaxis across Clark County, including Las Vegas, over the next 12 months.
articles.body:
Tesla, Uber and Waymo all got the green light on Thursday to operate thousands of robotaxis across Nevada. The state's transportation authority voted unanimously to authorise up to 8,000 vehicles in Clark County, which includes Las Vegas, over the next 12 months.

Tesla secured the largest allocation at 5,000 vehicles, though its chief engineer said that figure is a ceiling and the company realistically expects to deploy around 2,500. Waymo and Uber each received 1,000, with Uber running Motional and Zoox vehicles; Zoox's existing 100 robotaxis continue operating.

The decision follows an interim July permit that capped Tesla's fleet at ten vehicles, and marks a significant expansion of commercial robotaxi services in the Las Vegas area.

Local livery operators opposed the move, warning of overcrowding in the tourist district, but regulators said the phased rollout and safety requirements justified approval.

articles.headline: Jury finds Instagram and YouTube liable in landmark social media addiction trial
articles.subtitle: A Los Angeles jury has found Instagram and YouTube liable in a landmark social media addiction trial, recommending millions in damages — the second verdict against Meta this week after New Mexico's record $375 million penalty.
articles.body:
A jury in Los Angeles has found Instagram (Meta) and YouTube (Google) liable in a landmark social media addiction trial, the first of its kind to reach a verdict. After more than 40 hours of deliberations, jurors recommended millions in damages to a young plaintiff who argued the platforms were deliberately designed to be addictive.

The verdict follows another landmark ruling on Tuesday, when a New Mexico jury imposed a $375 million penalty on Meta after finding its platforms harmful to children's mental health, the largest such award yet.

Both companies vowed to appeal, arguing the platforms provide safeguards and that teens' social media use is shaped by many factors. Legal experts describe the cases as bellwethers for thousands of similar lawsuits filed by families across the US.

The rulings mark a pivotal moment for online safety litigation, with families of victims, including parents of children lost to sextortion schemes, hailing the decisions as long-overdue accountability.

articles.headline: Linux 7.2 released with cache-aware load balancing and Btrfs large folios
articles.subtitle: Linux 7.2 has been released with BPF improvements, cache-aware load balancing, large-folio support in Btrfs and better swap handling, after one of the busiest development cycles in the kernel's history.
articles.body:
Linus Torvalds released Linux 7.2 this weekend, wrapping up one of the busiest development cycles in the kernel's recent history. The release adds thousands of commits from hundreds of developers.

Notable changes include common attributes for the bpf() syscall, cache-aware load balancing in the CPU scheduler, large-folio support in Btrfs and a series of swap improvements, plus updates to Landlock and new inline encryption support via dm-inlinecrypt.

The release candidate series ran longer than usual, which Torvalds attributed to the sheer volume of changes and the summer merge window. Distributions will begin shipping 7.2 in the coming months.

As always, the kernel remains the largest collaborative software project on Earth, and 7.2's changelog reflects contributions from hobbyists and the world's biggest tech companies alike.

articles.headline: Framework responds after BIOS 3.20 update bricks Ryzen 7040 laptops
articles.subtitle: Framework says it will replace affected mainboards, including out-of-warranty ones, after complaints that a BIOS 3.20 update for the Laptop 13 with Ryzen 7040 chips has left some machines unable to boot.
articles.body:
Framework is responding to reports that a BIOS update has bricked some of its laptops. Users say upgrading to BIOS 3.20 on the Framework Laptop 13 with AMD Ryzen 7040 series processors can leave machines unable to boot, with reports dating back to March.

The company has confirmed the issue affects a subset of Ryzen 7040 boards and says it will replace mainboards for confirmed affected customers, including those whose warranties have expired.

Framework is investigating the root cause and has posted guidance on its community forum, urging affected users to contact support. The company stressed that the issue is limited to the Ryzen 7040 platform and does not affect other configurations.

The episode is a reminder of the risks of firmware updates, and Framework has pledged to review its release process to prevent a repeat.

articles.headline: ChatGPT can now send texts for you with a new Apple Messages plugin
articles.subtitle: ChatGPT can now read, search, draft and send messages through Apple's Messages app on Mac, in a new plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex users that runs locally with per-message approval prompts.
articles.body:
OpenAI is rolling out a plugin that lets ChatGPT and Codex work directly with Apple Messages on macOS. Available to ChatGPT Work and Codex users on Apple silicon Macs, the plugin can read, search, draft and send iMessage, SMS and RCS messages.

Every send requires approval, with Allow once and Always allow options, and the integration works locally via AppleScript and Accessibility APIs, meaning messages are not uploaded to OpenAI's servers.

The move raises interesting privacy questions: while the local approach is more private than cloud-based assistants, the plugin does require broad system access, and OpenAI notes users should consider what they permit ChatGPT to see.

The release continues OpenAI's push to embed ChatGPT into everyday workflows, following similar plugins for calendar, reminders and note-taking apps.

articles.headline: A tracked shipment of rare books ended up at an Amazon AI training facility
articles.subtitle: 404 Media tracked a shipment of 1,000 rare books — one fitted with an AirTag — from a bookseller to an Amazon warehouse in Las Vegas, where they were being destructively scanned, apparently to train AI.
articles.body:
A shipment of 1,000 rare books ordered through Biblio has ended up inside an Amazon facility in Las Vegas, where the books appear to be destructively scanned to train AI models. 404 Media's investigation planted an AirTag inside one of the books to follow the route.

The parcel travelled from the bookseller to Amazon's LAS8 warehouse, where it was handled by a team identified as VGT3. Footage and photos show workers tearing spines off books for high-speed scanning, a process that destroys them.

Booksellers have long suspected that companies are buying up every ISBN in print to build training datasets, and Amazon's own T-rex logo is visible in the operation, suggesting the scanning is happening inside the warehouse chain.

The practice has alarmed the rare-book trade: collectors fear the physical record is being destroyed for the benefit of AI, with no compensation to authors or publishers.

articles.headline: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users — and sharpening its privacy pitch
articles.subtitle: New data suggests OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic among business users, as the two labs sharpen their enterprise pitches: OpenAI is expanding customer privacy protections while Anthropic details how Claude's new watermarks will work.
articles.body:
The race for enterprise AI customers is tightening. New data indicates OpenAI is gaining ground on Anthropic in the business segment, a market Anthropic has long dominated thanks to Claude's coding strength and enterprise focus.

OpenAI is seeking to one-up its rival with new customer privacy protections, aiming to reassure enterprises that their data and models will not be used for training or shared with third parties.

Anthropic, meanwhile, has shared more details about how Claude's new content watermarks will work, positioning provenance and traceability as a selling point for businesses worried about liability and compliance.

Both companies are pouring resources into enterprise sales as consumer growth plateaus, and the next year will likely decide which lab becomes the default choice for corporate AI.
